picks.title: DeepMind takes 15 years of game AI research into EVE Online with Fenris Creations
picks.excerpt: DeepMind traces 15 years of game AI research from Atari agents to persistent online worlds, and announces a partnership with Fenris Creations to prototype AI agents inside the EVE Universe — a bid to turn research agents into shipped gameplay design.
picks.rationale: Research agents moving into a live persistent MMO is the clearest signal yet that agent behaviour becomes a design material, not a demo.

picks.title: Skillprint's Signal Benchmark scores how well AI can steer a player's mental state
picks.excerpt: Skillprint's Signal Benchmark scores how well AI models can shift players toward a target mental state, adjusting game parameters in real time — framing adaptive difficulty and pacing as a measurable, model-driven design layer.
picks.rationale: Turns pacing and difficulty tuning into a measurable target, which is exactly the hook a designer needs to argue for adaptive systems.

picks.title: Rainbow Six Siege cut critical toxic voice chat by 50% with Modulate's ToxMod
picks.excerpt: Ubisoft reports Rainbow Six Siege cut critical toxic voice chat by 50% using Modulate's ToxMod, with roughly 800,000 hours of voice audio analyzed monthly — AI moderation as a shipped part of live-service experience design.
picks.rationale: A hard shipped number on AI moderation at scale: community safety stops being policy talk and becomes a live-service design metric.

picks.title: Rez Graham and Luke Dicken on what actually matters about AI in game development
picks.excerpt: Former Maxis engineer David 'Rez' Graham and ex-Take-Two AI head Luke Dicken unpack what actually matters about AI in game development beyond the hype — separating classic game AI craft from generative tooling and its effect on the nature of the work.
picks.rationale: Two practitioners draw the line between game AI craft and generative tooling — the vocabulary you need before your team argues about either.

picks.title: Patrice Desilets defends AI imagery in 1666: Amsterdam: '75 different variations'
picks.excerpt: Patrice Desilets defends AI-generated imagery in 1666: Amsterdam's reveal, arguing 'I can ask the AI to give me 75 different variations' at a speed human illustrators couldn't match — a blunt statement of the iteration-vs-craft tradeoff.
picks.rationale: A named veteran director states the iteration-speed case out loud, which is the argument every art lead will have to answer this year.
